title: Flying Witch
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Makoto, a polite trainee witch from Yokohama, moves with her black cat familiar Chito to live with cousins in rural Hirosaki, Aomori, as part of her training. The episodic story follows her daily life as her relatives and new friends meet the customs of witchcraft, including her young cousin Chinatsu, who becomes an apprentice (Wikipedia; Kodansha blurb via AniList).
life_message: A gentle life of family, nature, seasons and small wonders is worth slowing down for.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No feuds; mild episodic comedy (MU Episodic, Warm Ambience).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Makoto trains at her own pace; Akane travels the world freely (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Story centers on cousins' household and sisters (Wikipedia; AniList Family Life).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Apprentice-teacher roles (Chinatsu under Akane) held lightly (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Inherited witch customs and rural dialect valued (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Iyashikei: quality of daily life over striving (AniList).

folkways.japan: Rural Aomori life, Tsugaru dialect and casual coexistence with spirits reflect Japanese regional and folk-religious culture.

delivery.evidence: Episodic slice-of-life with no stated lesson (Wikipedia; MU Episodic). No review opened (to verify).
delivery.note: The series presents witchcraft and rural life as normal rather than arguing for them, as far as summaries show.

winners_losers: No losers; Makoto, her family and new friends all gain. Sympathy goes to a gentle, nature-attuned witchcraft.
